source: English translation: Valmiki Ramayanam, IIT Kanpur (https://www.valmiki.iitk.ac.in/), via the MIT-licensed Valmiki Ramayan Dataset by Ashutosh Vijay.

verses.1: When that night had dawned, King Rama, the greatly effulgent one, having gone to the sacrificial enclosure, summoned all the sages.
verses.2: Vasistha, Vamadeva, Jabali, Kashyapa, Vishwamitra of great austerity, and Durvasa of great penance were present.
verses.3: Pulastya, Shakti, Bhargava, Vamana, the long-lived Markandeya, and the highly renowned Maudgalya were also present.
verses.4: Garga, Chyavana, Shatananda the knower of dharma, the radiant Bharadvaja, and the brilliant Agniputra were also among them.
verses.5: Narada, Parvata, the highly renowned Gautama, Katyayana, Suyajna, and Agastya, a treasure-house of austerities, were also present.
verses.6: These and many other sages of firm vows, all filled with curiosity, had assembled.
verses.7: All the great-souled demons of immense valor and monkeys of great strength assembled there out of curiosity.
verses.8: Thousands of Kshatriyas, Shudras, and Vaishyas, along with Brahmins of firm vows from various countries, also gathered.
verses.9: All these, including those devoted to knowledge, action, and yoga, had assembled there to witness Sita's oath.
verses.10: Then, hearing that everyone had assembled and stood unmoving like a stone, the best of sages, Valmiki, quickly approached with Sita.
verses.11: Sita, with a downcast face, folded hands, and a voice choked with tears, followed that sage from behind, having fixed Rama in her mind.
verses.12: Upon seeing Sita following Valmiki, appearing like a Veda following Brahma, a great acclamation of "excellent" arose from the crowd.
verses.13: Then, a tumultuous clamor arose from all those whose minds were agitated by the vast sorrow born of their distress.
verses.14: Some spectators acclaimed, "Excellent, Rama!", others cried, "Excellent, Sita!", and still others there loudly praised both of them.
verses.15: Then, having entered the midst of the multitude of people, Valmiki, the foremost of sages, accompanied by Sita, spoke thus to Rama.
verses.16: O son of Dasharatha, this is Sita, virtuous and righteous, who was abandoned near my hermitage due to public slanders.
verses.17: O Rama, keeper of great vows, you who are fearful of public scandal, Sita will provide proof, and you ought to permit her to do so.
verses.18: These two formidable sons, born as twins to Janaki, are indeed your own sons, and I speak this truth to you.
verses.19: O delight of the Raghus, I am the tenth son of Prachetas, and I have never uttered a lie; these two are indeed your sons.
verses.20: If this Maithili were impure, I would not partake of the fruit of the penance that I have performed for many thousands of years.
verses.21: If Maithili is sinless, then may I enjoy the fruit of never having committed any sin by thought, word, or deed.
verses.22: O Raghava, I, who am present in the five elements and the mind as the sixth, accepted Sita as pure, having considered her in the forest stream.
verses.23: This Sita, who is of pure conduct, sinless, and devoted to her husband as a deity, will provide conviction to you, who feared public scandal.
verses.24: Therefore, O son of the best among men, this Sita of pure nature, whom you, whose mind was defiled by public scandal, abandoned even though she was known to be pure and dearest to you, then entered the divine realm. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे षण्णवतितमः सर्गः ।। 96 ।। Thus ends the ninety-sixth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
